nodes.name: In-MIL-68 solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 720 mg 1,4-benzene dicarboxylic acid (H2BDC) and 720 mg indium nitrate hydrate (In(NO3)3·xH2O) were dissolved in 480 mL N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF), and vigorously stirred for 10 min. Then, the solution was heated to 120°C and stirred for 1 h. When the temperature decreased to RT, the white precipitation was collected by centrifuging and washed with DMF and absolute ethanol three times, denoted as In-MIL-68 prisms.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, 720 mg 1,4-benzene dicarboxylic acid (H2BDC) and 720 mg indium nitrate hydrate... washed with DMF and absolute ethanol three times, denoted as In-MIL-68 prisms.

nodes.name: In2O3 microtubes thermal treatment
nodes.procedure: The In2O3 microtubes were obtained by annealing In-MIL-68 prisms at 120°C for 2 h and 500°C for 4 h in sequence with a 5°C/min heating rate.

nodes.name: MoS2 nanoflakes solvothermal growth
nodes.procedure: 50.42 mg sodium molybdate dihydrate (Na2MoO4·2H2O), 71.25 mg thiourea ((NH2)2CS) were added into 20 mL deionized (DI) water under continuous stirring. After 30 min, 100 mg as-synthesized In2O3 microtubes were added to the above mixture and vigorously stirred for another 30 min. Afterward, the mixture was poured into a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave with heating at 200°C for 24 h. When the temperature declined to RT, the product was achieved through filtration, washing with DI water and absolute ethanol, and drying at 60°C in a vacuum dryer for 8 h. The product was indicated as In2O3@MoS2; here, the weight percentage of MoS2 is 25%. For investigating the effect of MoS2 amount on the sensing response, the other two samples with 10% and 50% MoS2 were fabricated by adjusting the amount of added MoS2 precursors and denoted as In2O3@MoS2-I and In2O3@MoS2-II, respectively.

nodes.description: Stability testing - repeatability to 1 ppm NO₂ at RT
nodes.source_text: Fig. 10(a) demonstrates three successive cycle response tests on the In₂O₃@MoS₂ gas sensor to 1 ppm NO₂ at RT. During these cycles, the initial resistances of the In₂O₃@MoS₂ sensor keep identical, and the changes in response are below 4%

nodes.description: Long-term stability testing to 1 ppm NO₂ at RT over 50 days
nodes.source_text: Fig. 10(b) presents the response of the In₂O₃@MoS₂ sensor to 1 ppm NO₂ at RT in 50 days. The result shows that the In₂O₃@MoS₂ sensor has good stability, and the largest standard deviation (SD) was less than 2%

The sensing response of the In₂O₃@MoS₂ sensor toward various interfering gas, including carbon monoxide (CO), ammonia (NH₃), hydrogen sulfide (H₂S), and methane (CH₄), at RT was measured to evaluate the sensor's selectivity for NO₂. As presented in Fig. 10(c), the response toward NO₂ is distinctly higher than the others

nodes.description: Humidity effect testing to 1 ppm NO₂ at different RH levels
nodes.source_text: Fig. 11 shows the transient response/recovery curves of the In₂O₃@MoS₂ sensor to 1 ppm NO₂ with different RH conditions. As shown in the figures, the responses decrease with the increase of RH

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks at 21.4°, 30.6°, 35.5°, 51.0°, and 60.5° ascribed to (211), (222), (400), (440), and (622) crystal faces of cubic In₂O₃; peaks at 14.3°, 33.2°, 39.2°, and 58.6° attributed to (002), (101), (103), and (110) planes of 2H-MoS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction peaks of 21.4°, 30.6°, 35.5°, 51.0°, and 60.5°, can be ascribed to the (211), (222), (400), (440), and (622) crystal faces of cubic structured In₂O₃ ... peaks of sample MoS₂ at 14.3°, 33.2°, 39.2°, and 58.6° are attributed to the (002), (101), (103), and (110) crystal planes of pure MoS₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: In₂O₃@MoS₂ shows In 3d₅/₂ 444.70 eV, 3d₃/₂ 452.27 eV (In³⁺); Mo 3d₅/₂ 229.1 eV, 3d₃/₂ 232.2 eV (Mo⁴⁺), Mo⁶⁺ at 235.5 eV; S 2p₃/₂ 161.8 eV, 2p₁/₂ 163.2 eV (S²⁻); O 1s: O_L 11.32%, O_V 17.17% (increased from 7.81%), O_C 71.51% (increased from 52.98%) vs pristine In₂O₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic peaks at 444.70 eV and 452.27 eV are derived from the In 3d₅/₂ and In 3d₃/₂ ... two strong peaks at 229.1 and 232.2 eV are attributed to Mo 3d₅/₂ and Mo 3d₃/₂ peaks of the lower oxidation state of Mo⁴⁺ from MoS₂ ... peaks at 161.8 and 163.2 eV of the S element belong to the S²⁻ 2p₃/₂ and S²⁻ 2p₁/₂ ... the ratio of O_C, O_V, O_L in pristine In₂O₃ and In₂O₃@MoS₂ ... O_C and O_V increased from 52.98% to 71.51% and from 7.81% to 17.17%, respectively.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The isotherms can be categorized to type IV isotherms with H1-type hysteresis loops ... The BET-specific surface areas of In₂O₃ and In₂O₃@MoS₂ are 40.84 and 53.44 m²/g, respectively ... the pore size in In₂O₃@MoS₂ (3-10 nm) is larger than that of In₂O₃ (2 nm).
